title: What a determinant measures: how much area grows

explain.say: Start with a little square, 1 unit by 1 unit. Its area is 1. Look at the first bar. When a matrix moves the plane, this square turns into a new shape. The determinant tells you its new area.

explain.say: Stretch across by 2 and up by 3. The square becomes a 2 by 3 rectangle with area 6. Look at the second bar. The determinant is 2 times 3, which is 6. Every shape on the grid gets 6 times bigger!

explain.say: 1! For any 2 by 2 matrix a, b, c, d, the determinant is a d minus b c. For 3, 1 and 1, 2 that is 3 times 2 minus 1 times 1, which is 5. Look at the last bar: area 5.

faq.q: What does the determinant of a matrix mean?
faq.a: It is the area scale factor. A matrix with determinant 6 makes every shape 6 times bigger in area. A negative determinant also flips the shape over.

faq.q: Why does a shear have determinant 1?
faq.a: A shear slides layers sideways like a deck of cards. The base and height do not change, so the area stays the same and the determinant is 1.
asks: Why does a shear keep area?

faq.q: How do you work out a 2 by 2 determinant?
faq.a: For the matrix a, b on top and c, d below, the determinant is a times d minus b times c.

faq.q: What does a determinant of zero mean?
faq.a: The matrix squashes the plane onto a line or a point, so areas become zero. You cannot undo it, so the matrix has no inverse. It is called singular.

faq.q: What does a negative determinant mean?
faq.a: The shape is flipped over, like a mirror image, as well as being scaled. The size of the number is still the area scale factor.

facts: The determinant of the 2×2 matrix with rows (a, b) and (c, d) is ad − bc.
The absolute value of a 2×2 determinant is the factor by which the matrix scales area.
